title: [CQ-RF06b] VS Code protected daemon spawn
description:
Objective: under the protected profile, the VS Code extension starts the Moe daemon only from the runtime installed with the extension. This mirrors JetBrains MoeDaemonSupervisor.protectedDaemonCommand / protectedDaemonEnvironment / protectedCommandOrRefuse. Split out of CQ-RF06 (task-98ffe33f448746e6bc802db0b5624fd0) by architect-bd1eb82d on 2026-10-30 to keep each diff under the 400-LOC review cap. RF06 lands the shared policy as exported functions in moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts: runtimeProfile (strict, fail-closed, session pin), comparablePath/isWithin, installedRoot(extensionPath) = <extensionPath>/bundled and installedArtifact. This row consumes them in the same file.

Deliverable: when runtimeProfile(projectPath) is 'protected', MoeDaemonClient.startDaemon:
1. Selects the daemon with installedArtifact(installedRoot, 'daemon/index.js', projectPath). resolveGlobalConfigDaemonPath and any project copy are never consulted.
2. Selects node as an absolute, real, regular file outside the project (a mirror of JetBrains installedExecutable). It tries, in this order:
   - MOE_NODE_COMMAND;
   - on non-Windows, ~/.local/share/moe/node/current/bin/node;
   - an in-process lookup of node or node.exe over PATH entries that are absolute and outside the project (never a bare name resolved by spawn);
   - on Windows, the resolveNodeExecutable candidates (ProgramFiles, ProgramFiles(x86), LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\nodejs, LOCALAPPDATA\nvm\current, APPDATA\nvm).
3. Spawns [node, daemon, 'start', '--project', projectPath] with cwd = the installed daemon's directory. The env drops NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH, and PATH (matched case-insensitively on Windows) keeps only absolute entries outside the project.
4. Refuses instead of falling back: any rejection starts nothing, logs the reason and shows `Protected execution profile: <reason>. Project and PATH copies of the Moe daemon are not used.`
5. The legacy profile is byte-for-byte unchanged.

Out of scope:
- Running-daemon provenance (JetBrains activationRefusal, spawn records, RF03 replacement). VS Code under protected still connects to an existing daemon.json daemon. Node has no portable process start-time API, so this stays a known gap, recorded for CQ-RF07.
- Persistent state, JetBrains changes, .moe edits, enabling verified-local.

Constraint: five test harnesses (daemon-start, daemon-json-cap, approval-paths, plan-approval-client, settings-wire) transpile MoeDaemonClient.ts alone with a closed require shim. Add no new local runtime import to MoeDaemonClient.ts.

Verification command (fresh, exit 0 required): cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile
definitionOfDone: Under the protected profile, startDaemon spawns exactly [real node outside the project, real installed bundled/daemon/index.js, 'start', '--project', projectPath], with cwd = the installed daemon dir and an env without NODE_OPTIONS, NODE_PATH or relative/project PATH entries. Shown by tests in a new moe-vscode/tests/*.test.cjs.

Under the protected profile, a missing installed daemon, or no acceptable node, spawns nothing, shows the 'Protected execution profile: … Project and PATH copies of the Moe daemon are not used.' refusal, and never consults the global-config daemon. Shown by tests.
The legacy profile behaves exactly as before: the existing daemon-start tests pass unchanged.
The verification command exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.

Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Under the protected execution profile, the VS Code extension starts the Moe daemon only from the runtime installed with the extension: the real bundled/daemon/index.js, run by a real node executable outside the project, with 'start' and cwd = the installed daemon dir. The env drops NODE_OPTIONS and NODE_PATH, and PATH keeps only fully qualified entries outside the project, spelled as validated. On a Windows host, containment is decided only between plain local drive paths. A path form is a Windows alias unless it is drive-qualified (X:\, optionally behind a \\?\ prefix) and no segment ends in '.' or ' '. So UNC, volume-device, rooted and drive-relative forms are aliases. A candidate with an alias form (resolved spelling or real path) is never outside the project. A project base with an alias form (raw spelling, resolved spelling or real path) leaves nothing provably outside it and gets no installed file. Examples are a UNC or \\wsl$ workspace, a mapped network drive, a rooted spelling and a link to a literal 'project.' folder. For such a base, startDaemon spawns nothing and shows 'Protected execution profile: the project directory is not a plain local Windows path. Project and PATH copies of the Moe daemon are not used.' A reachable and an unreachable share get the same refusal. Any rejection starts nothing and shows the standard refusal. The legacy profile and POSIX hosts are unchanged.

invariants: Under protected, nothing is spawned unless both the daemon and node are accepted
Refusal messages carry reasons only; absolute paths go to the log

On a Windows host, every kept PATH entry, every accepted real path and every project form used for containment is a plain local drive path. It reads identically under Node's literal fs and under the Win32 normalization the OS applies to spawn and to PATH search

A project base with any alias form keeps no PATH entry and accepts no installed file. Its raw spelling is checked before any filesystem call, so an unreachable share gets the same refusal as a reachable one
Host semantics: the Windows alias rule applies only when process.platform is win32, never through the windows argument that tests pass on Linux for env-key casing
compatibility: The legacy profile keeps resolveBundledDaemonPath || resolveGlobalConfigDaemonPath, resolveDaemonRuntime, 'init' with --name, and the exact spawn options {detached, stdio, windowsHide, env}

POSIX hosts: trailing dots and spaces stay literal name characters, '//' paths are not UNC, and relative bases keep today's behavior; no new refusal

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Three shapes for the inverse-UNC reject.
(1) Refuse only a UNC base. It closes QA's repro but keeps enumerating spelling classes: a rooted base or another namespace would be round 4, and the reopen cap is spent.
(2) Identity containment: compare dev+ino of the candidate and each ancestor against the project root, the governor's first direction. It would also close the nonexistent-leaf gap. Rejected for this row: it means rewriting isOutsideProject and pathForms (the rail forbids rewriting landed bytes), it blows the size budget, and SMB file IDs would need their own probe. It is a candidate for later hardening.
(3) Chosen: the governor's second direction, fail closed outside one namespace. isWindowsAlias becomes an allow-list (a plain local drive path) and applies to both sides: the candidate's forms, and the base's raw, resolved and real forms. That is +2 net source lines. The architect validated the exact diff on native Windows (D:\moe-rf06b-r3-architect-probe): RED on e83fef4c, GREEN with the patch, all six mutants killed, QA's three repros clean, net 459 total.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: selectInstalledFile serves installedArtifact (RF06's wrapper, daemon and proxy, also via AgentLauncher.ts) and installedExecutable. isOutsideProject feeds protectedPathEntries, which feeds nodeOnProtectedPath and protectedDaemonEnvironment. comparablePath strips the \\?\ and \\.\ prefixes and maps \\?\UNC\ to //. The '.' device segment of a \\.\ form is already caught by the dot regex. getWorkspacePath returns uri.fsPath unchanged. runtimeProfile treats a non-ENOENT lstat error as protected (fail closed), so an unreachable UNC base still reaches the protected branch, where the raw-spelling check refuses it.
